doctrines.question: How far does Scripture's truthfulness extend?
doctrines.framing: Everyone in this conversation holds that Scripture is true. The question is the range of that claim - whether it covers history and cosmology as well as faith and salvation.
doctrines.tier_note: The authority of Scripture is the ground every other doctrine is argued from.

open.todo: Work out whether inerrancy extends to history and science or only to what Scripture teaches for salvation.

positions.label: Full inerrancy
positions.hold: Scripture is without error in all that it affirms, including what it affirms about history and the created order.
positions.why: Scripture's self-attestation treats it as true in what it asserts, not only in what it teaches for salvation.
positions.vs: Limited infallibility - Scripture trustworthy on faith and salvation, errant on history and science.

positions.label: Limited infallibility
positions.hold: Scripture is wholly trustworthy in what it teaches for salvation, and speaks of history and the natural world in the terms of its own age.
positions.why: The purpose for which Scripture was given sets the range of the claim its truthfulness makes.

doctrines.question: Which books belong to Scripture, and on what basis?
doctrines.framing: The question is both which books the church received and what made them receivable - whether the church conferred authority on them or recognised an authority already there.
doctrines.tier_note: Which books count is prior to any argument made from them.

open.todo: Work out what the church was doing when it recognised the canon, and whether the deuterocanonical books belong inside it or beside it.

positions.label: Sixty-six books
positions.hold: The canon is the sixty-six books of the Protestant Bible, recognised by the church rather than conferred by it.
positions.why: Authority belongs to the books because of their origin, and the church's role was to receive what was already given.

positions.label: With deuterocanon
positions.hold: The canon includes the deuterocanonical books received by the church from the earliest centuries and confirmed by council.
positions.why: The books the church read as Scripture in its worship are the books the church holds as Scripture.

sources.label: Council of Trent
sources.citation: Session IV, Decree on Sacred Books (1546)
